intent.raw_query: Morocco Marrakech and Sahara, $1000 solo, 7 days, March

experiences.name: Djemaa el-Fna Square & Medina Exploration
experiences.description: Immerse yourself in the beating heart of Marrakech by wandering the UNESCO-listed Djemaa el-Fna square. Watch snake charmers, storytellers, and musicians by day, then stay for the magical transformation at dusk when food stalls fill the air with smoke and spices. Explore the labyrinthine souks of the surrounding medina, bargaining for spices, leather goods, and handwoven textiles.

experiences.name: Sahara Desert Camel Trek & Overnight Camp
experiences.description: Journey to the golden dunes of Erg Chebbi near Merzouga and embark on a sunset camel trek into the Sahara. Spend the night in a traditional Berber camp under a breathtaking canopy of stars, enjoy live Gnawa music around a campfire, sip mint tea, and wake before dawn to witness a spectacular desert sunrise over the dunes.

experiences.name: Traditional Moroccan Cooking Class
experiences.description: Join a local chef in a riad kitchen for a hands-on cooking class where you learn to prepare authentic Moroccan dishes such as lamb tagine with preserved lemon, harira soup, and honey-drenched pastilla. Begin with a guided tour of the spice souks to source fresh ingredients like ras el hanout, saffron, and argan oil before cooking and dining together.

experiences.name: Bahia Palace & Saadian Tombs Historical Tour
experiences.description: Step back into the grandeur of Moroccan imperial history with a self-guided or locally led tour of the 19th-century Bahia Palace, adorned with intricate zellige tilework, carved cedarwood ceilings, and lush courtyards. Continue to the nearby Saadian Tombs, a hidden necropolis of the 16th-century Saadian dynasty rediscovered in 1917, featuring stunning marble and stucco craftsmanship.

experiences.name: Ksar of Aït Benhaddou & Draa Valley Drive
experiences.description: Travel through the dramatic Atlas Mountain passes to the UNESCO World Heritage ksar (fortified village) of Aït Benhaddou, a stunning example of southern Moroccan earthen clay architecture and a famous film location for Gladiator and Game of Thrones. Continue into the lush Draa Valley, dotted with ancient kasbahs, date palm oases, and Berber villages, stopping for a traditional lunch of mechoui (slow-roasted lamb) at a local auberge.
experiences.location: Aït Benhaddou & Draa Valley, Ouarzazate Province

trip_options.title: Budget Explorer - Morocco – Marrakech and Sahara
trip_options.description: Save money without sacrificing the experience. Perfect for travelers who value authentic local experiences over luxury.

day_by_day.morning: N/A – Flight arrives at 22:30
day_by_day.afternoon: N/A – In transit
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at Marrakech Menara Airport at 22:30. Take the 19 bus or a shared petit taxi (negotiate firmly, ~50–70 MAD) to Hotel Aday in the Medina. Check in, freshen up, and take a short stroll around the quiet night streets of Derb Sidi Bouloukat to get your bearings.

meals.breakfast: On the plane
meals.lunch: On the plane or airport snack
meals.dinner: Grab a quick late-night snack from a street cart near Jemaa el-Fna square (msemen flatbread or harira soup, ~10–15 MAD) if still open on your walk from the taxi drop-off.

day_by_day.notes: Keep some small MAD bills ready for the taxi. Avoid unofficial 'guides' at the airport. Hotel Aday is a budget riad-style guesthouse in the heart of the Medina – confirm your late arrival with them in advance. Rest well; big day tomorrow.

day_by_day.morning: Start with a traditional Moroccan breakfast at the hotel or a nearby café (mint tea, msemen, amlou almond-argan dip, ~20–30 MAD). Then walk 10 minutes to the iconic Jemaa el-Fna square to soak in the morning atmosphere – orange juice vendors, snake charmers setting up, and locals heading to work. Explore the Koutoubia Mosque gardens (exterior free) and the surrounding souks: Souk Semmarine (textiles), Souk des Épices (spice market). Bargain respectfully – first prices are always inflated.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Bahia Palace (entrance ~70 MAD), a stunning 19th-century palace with ornate Moroccan architecture, carved cedar ceilings, and lush courtyards. Afterward, walk to the Mellah (Jewish Quarter) and the nearby El Badi Palace ruins (entrance ~70 MAD) for panoramic rooftop views and nesting storks. Both are within 15 minutes' walk of the hotel.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Jemaa el-Fna at dusk when it transforms into a massive open-air food festival. Eat dinner at the communal food stalls (stalls 1–100 area) – try merguez sausages, kefta brochettes, snail soup (babouche), and fresh-squeezed orange juice. Budget ~50–80 MAD for a full meal. Watch the Gnawa musicians, storytellers, and acrobats perform for free.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or café near Derb Sidi Bouloukat – mint tea, msemen, honey (~20–30 MAD)
meals.lunch: Street food in the souks – a bowl of harira soup + bread at a local snack stand (~15–20 MAD)
meals.dinner: Jemaa el-Fna night market food stalls – kefta, merguez, salads, orange juice (~50–80 MAD)

day_by_day.notes: Wear comfortable walking shoes. The Medina streets are narrow and maze-like – download an offline map (Maps.me or Google Maps offline). Politely decline 'free' guided tours from strangers in the souks as they always end at a shop with pressure to buy.

day_by_day.morning: Early morning visit to the Saadian Tombs (entrance ~70 MAD) – a beautifully preserved 16th-century royal necropolis hidden for centuries. Arrive before 9:00 AM to beat crowds. Then walk to the nearby Kasbah Mosque (exterior only) and explore the Kasbah neighborhood, one of Marrakech's oldest quarters. Stop at a local bakery (farran) to buy fresh-baked khobz bread (~2 MAD per loaf).
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to the Jardin Majorelle (entrance ~100 MAD for garden, +100 MAD for Berber Museum) – the iconic cobalt-blue garden once owned by Yves Saint Laurent. It's about a 25-minute walk or a 10 MAD bus ride (Line 11) from the Medina. Alternatively, if budget is tight, visit the free Cyber Park (Arset el Harti) or the public Menara Gardens (free entry, pavilion ~10 MAD) for a relaxing afternoon among olive groves and a reflective pool.
day_by_day.evening: Explore the northern souks at golden hour – Souk Haddadine (blacksmiths), Souk Cherratin (leather workers), and Souk Smata (babouche slippers). Watch artisans at work for free. Have dinner at a local restaurant away from the main square for better prices – try Restaurant Souk Kafe or any small derb restaurant for a set menu tagine (~60–80 MAD).

meals.breakfast: Fresh msemen with honey and argan oil at a neighborhood café (~25 MAD)
meals.lunch: Sandwich marocain (kefta or tuna baguette) from a street stall near Majorelle (~20–25 MAD)
meals.dinner: Local Medina restaurant – chicken or lamb tagine with bread and mint tea (~60–80 MAD)

day_by_day.notes: The Jardin Majorelle can be skipped if very budget-conscious (200 MAD total is significant). The Menara Gardens offer a peaceful free alternative. Wednesday markets in the Medina are lively – great for people-watching.

day_by_day.morning: Early wake-up at 5:30–6:00 AM. Pack an overnight bag for the Sahara (2 nights). Join a shared budget group tour to Merzouga/Erg Chebbi dunes – book in advance through your hotel or a local agency (budget shared tours: ~600–900 MAD per person for a 3-day/2-night trip including transport, accommodation, and camel ride). Depart Marrakech around 7:00 AM. The route passes through the dramatic Tizi n'Tichka mountain pass (2,260m) in the High Atlas.
day_by_day.afternoon: Stop in Ouarzazate ('the door of the desert') for lunch and a brief visit to the Kasbah Taourirt (entrance ~20 MAD) – a UNESCO-listed earthen fortress. Continue through the Valley of Roses (Dades Valley) and the Draa Valley, passing ancient kasbahs, palm oases, and Berber villages. The landscape shifts dramatically from mountains to pre-Saharan plains.
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at Merzouga village (gateway to Erg Chebbi dunes) around 18:00–19:00. Mount camels at sunset for a 45-minute ride into the dunes to your desert camp. Watch the sun set over the orange sand dunes of Erg Chebbi (up to 150m high). Enjoy a Berber dinner at camp under a sky full of stars – no light pollution here. Traditional music around the campfire.

meals.breakfast: Quick breakfast at hotel before departure – bread, olive oil, tea (~20 MAD or included in hotel)
meals.lunch: Lunch stop in Ouarzazate – local restaurant set menu: harira, tagine, tea (~50–70 MAD)
meals.dinner: Included in desert camp package – traditional Berber meal: tagine, couscous, mint tea

day_by_day.notes: Book your Sahara group tour at least 1–2 days in advance. Shared minibus tours are the most budget-friendly option. Bring warm layers – desert nights in March can drop to 5–10°C. Bring a headlamp, sunscreen, sunglasses, and a scarf/shemagh for sand. Charge all devices before leaving Marrakech.

day_by_day.morning: Wake before sunrise (around 6:00 AM) to climb the dunes for a breathtaking Sahara sunrise – one of the most memorable experiences in Morocco. The silence and colors are extraordinary. After sunrise, return to camp for a Berber breakfast (mint tea, bread, olive oil, honey, eggs). Spend the morning sandboarding down the dunes (boards often available at camp), exploring the dune landscape on foot, or simply relaxing and reading.
day_by_day.afternoon: Camel ride or 4x4 excursion back to Merzouga village. Visit the local Merzouga village market and the small Gnawa music community (Khamlia village, ~10 km away) where descendants of sub-Saharan slaves maintain ancient musical traditions – a free and deeply cultural experience. Relax at a budget auberge in Merzouga with a rooftop terrace overlooking the dunes.
day_by_day.evening: Optional second night in the desert camp OR stay in a budget auberge in Merzouga (~100–150 MAD for a dorm/basic room). Watch the stars again from the rooftop. Have dinner at a local Merzouga restaurant – fresh tagine and Berber bread baked in sand (~50–70 MAD). Chat with fellow travelers and your Berber guides about desert life.

meals.breakfast: Included in desert camp – Berber breakfast: mint tea, bread, olive oil, honey, eggs
meals.lunch: Light lunch at Merzouga auberge or local café – omelette sandwich or tagine (~30–50 MAD)
meals.dinner: Local Merzouga restaurant – lamb or vegetable tagine with khobz bread (~50–70 MAD)

day_by_day.notes: The Khamlia village Gnawa music experience is a hidden gem – ask your guide to take you there. It's authentic, free (small tip appreciated), and deeply moving. Stay hydrated in the desert. March weather in the Sahara: warm days (~25–30°C), cold nights (~5–10°C).

day_by_day.morning: Early departure from Merzouga around 7:00–8:00 AM for the long return journey to Marrakech (approximately 9–10 hours with stops). Pass through the Todra Gorge if your tour includes it – a spectacular 300m-high canyon carved by the Todra River. Walk through the narrow gorge floor (free) and have tea at a local café inside the gorge (~15 MAD).
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue through the Dades Gorge ('Road of a Thousand Kasbahs') with stops at roadside Berber villages and earthen kasbahs. Lunch stop in Boumalne Dades or Kelaa M'Gouna (Rose Valley) – try a local cooperative restaurant for an affordable set menu. The landscape of rose fields (blooming in May, but still scenic in March) and ancient fortified villages is stunning.
day_by_day.evening: Arrive back in Marrakech around 18:00–19:00. Drop bags at Hotel Aday. Freshen up and head to Jemaa el-Fna for a final evening in the square. Treat yourself to a sit-down dinner at a slightly nicer local restaurant (still budget-friendly) – try pastilla (sweet pigeon pie) or a full Moroccan feast with bissara (fava bean soup) starter (~80–100 MAD). Enjoy the square's energy one last time.

meals.breakfast: Quick breakfast at Merzouga auberge before departure – bread, tea (~20 MAD or included)
meals.lunch: Set menu at a local cooperative restaurant in Dades/Boumalne – tagine + salad + tea (~50–70 MAD)
meals.dinner: Sit-down local restaurant near Jemaa el-Fna – pastilla or full Moroccan set menu (~80–100 MAD)

day_by_day.notes: The return journey is long but scenic – bring snacks, water, a book, and a portable charger. Todra Gorge is a highlight; confirm with your tour operator if it's included. If you feel stiff from the journey, a traditional hammam near the hotel (public hammam: ~15–30 MAD) is a perfect recovery option tonight.

day_by_day.morning: Leisurely final morning. Visit a traditional public hammam (Hammam Dar el-Bacha or a local neighborhood hammam near the hotel, ~15–50 MAD) for a steam bath and kessa scrub – an authentic Moroccan cultural experience. Afterward, explore any remaining souks or neighborhoods you missed: the Mouassine neighborhood (beautiful 16th-century fountain), the Chrob ou Chouf fountain, and the Ben Youssef Medersa (entrance ~70 MAD) – a stunning 14th-century Islamic college with intricate zellige tilework and carved stucco.
day_by_day.afternoon: Final souvenir shopping in the souks – best buys on a budget: argan oil, ras el hanout spice mix, leather goods, hand-painted ceramics, and woven textiles. Bargain hard (start at 30–40% of asking price). Visit the Cooperative Artisanale (fixed-price government shop) first to understand fair prices before bargaining in the souks. Enjoy a final mint tea on a rooftop café overlooking the Medina (~15–20 MAD).
day_by_day.evening: Check out of Hotel Aday (store luggage if needed). Final dinner at a local Medina restaurant – try a classic Moroccan couscous (traditionally served on Fridays but available Sunday too) or a mechoui (slow-roasted lamb) from the Rahba Kedima area (~60–80 MAD). Head to the airport – allow 45–60 minutes from the Medina. Take the 19 bus (~4 MAD) or a petit taxi (~50–70 MAD negotiated).

meals.breakfast: Final Moroccan breakfast at a neighborhood café – msemen, beghrir (honeycomb pancakes), mint tea (~25–35 MAD)
meals.lunch: Rooftop café near Ben Youssef Medersa – Moroccan salads, kefta sandwich, fresh juice (~40–60 MAD)
meals.dinner: Local Medina restaurant – couscous royale or mechoui lamb with bread and tea (~60–80 MAD)

day_by_day.notes: Ben Youssef Medersa is one of the most beautiful buildings in Morocco – don't miss it on your last day. Confirm your departure flight time and allow extra time for airport security. The 19 bus to the airport is the cheapest option but takes longer; a taxi is faster. Exchange any remaining MAD back to your currency at the airport (rates are worse there, so spend MAD on last-minute food/souvenirs instead).

trip_options.title: Classic Morocco – Marrakech and Sahara Experience
trip_options.description: The sweet spot between comfort and value. Enjoy quality accommodations, diverse experiences, and good food.

day_by_day.morning: N/A – Flight arrives at 22:30
day_by_day.afternoon: N/A – In transit
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at Marrakech Menara Airport at 22:30. Take a pre-arranged airport transfer or petit taxi (~80–100 MAD) to Hotel Aday in the Medina. Check in, freshen up, and take a short relaxed stroll around the immediate Derb Sidi Bouloukat alleyways to get your first feel of the Medina atmosphere.

meals.breakfast: On the plane
meals.lunch: On the plane or at the airport
meals.dinner: Light late-night snack at a nearby 24-hour café or grab street food near Jemaa el-Fna square (a 10-minute walk) – try a bowl of harira soup and msemen flatbread for ~20–30 MAD

day_by_day.notes: Keep Day 1 very light. Confirm your hotel has 24-hour reception. Exchange some currency at the airport (ATMs available). Rest well – big days ahead.

day_by_day.morning: After breakfast at the hotel, head to the iconic Jemaa el-Fna square (10-min walk) to soak in the morning atmosphere. Then explore the Koutoubia Mosque gardens and exterior. Continue into the historic souks – wander through the spice souk (Rahba Kedima), leather souk, and the dyers' quarter. Hire a local guide from the square for ~150–200 MAD for a 2-hour souk tour to avoid getting lost and gain cultural context.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the stunning Bahia Palace (entry ~70 MAD) – a 19th-century masterpiece of Moroccan architecture with ornate tilework and carved cedar ceilings. Afterward, walk to the nearby Mellah (Jewish Quarter) and explore the historic Lazama Synagogue. Stop at Place des Ferblantiers to admire the lantern craftsmen at work.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Jemaa el-Fna as it transforms into a vibrant open-air spectacle – snake charmers, storytellers, musicians, and food stalls. Enjoy dinner at one of the square's open-air grill stalls or at a rooftop restaurant overlooking the action.

meals.breakfast: At Hotel Aday or a nearby café – Moroccan mint tea, msemen, honey, and amlou (argan oil dip) for ~30–50 MAD
meals.lunch: Café des Épices in Rahba Kedima square – tagine or kefta sandwich with fresh juice for ~80–120 MAD
meals.dinner: Jemaa el-Fna food stalls – grilled merguez sausages, brochettes, and snail soup for ~60–100 MAD, or sit-down at Le Marrakchi rooftop restaurant for ~150–200 MAD

day_by_day.notes: Wear comfortable walking shoes. The souks can be overwhelming – stay calm, feel free to browse without obligation to buy. Bargaining is expected; start at 40–50% of the asking price.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Saadian Tombs (entry ~70 MAD) – a beautifully preserved 16th-century royal necropolis hidden for centuries. Then walk to the El Badi Palace ruins (entry ~70 MAD), a once-magnificent 16th-century palace now an atmospheric ruin with storks nesting on the ramparts and panoramic views from the top.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to the Majorelle Garden and YSL Museum (entry ~150 MAD combined) – a stunning cobalt-blue botanical garden once owned by Yves Saint Laurent, filled with exotic cacti and fountains. Afterward, explore the Gueliz neighborhood (New City) for a change of pace – browse art galleries and modern Moroccan boutiques along Avenue Mohammed V.
day_by_day.evening: Attend a traditional Moroccan hammam experience near the Medina – try Hammam Dar el-Bacha or a mid-range local hammam (~100–150 MAD for the full scrub and soap treatment). End the evening with a relaxed dinner in the Medina.

meals.breakfast: At the hotel or Café du Grand Balcon near Jemaa el-Fna – coffee, orange juice, and Moroccan pancakes for ~40–60 MAD
meals.lunch: Lunch near Majorelle Garden – Café Kif Kif or a nearby restaurant for a vegetable couscous or pastilla (pigeon pie) for ~100–150 MAD
meals.dinner: Riad Yima restaurant in the Medina – creative Moroccan cuisine in an artistic riad setting for ~150–200 MAD

day_by_day.notes: Book the Majorelle Garden online in advance as it sells out, especially in spring. The hammam is a must-do cultural experience – bring flip-flops and a change of clothes.

day_by_day.morning: Early departure (around 07:00) on a pre-booked 3-day/2-night Sahara Desert tour departing from Marrakech. The route heads southeast over the dramatic Tizi n'Tichka mountain pass (2,260m) through the High Atlas Mountains. Stop at the UNESCO-listed Aït Benhaddou ksar – a stunning fortified mud-brick village used in films like Gladiator and Game of Thrones. Explore the kasbah on foot with a local guide (~1.5 hours).
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue driving through the Draa Valley – a lush palm-lined oasis cutting through arid desert landscape. Stop at Ouarzazate (the 'Hollywood of Morocco') for a brief visit to the Atlas Film Studios (entry ~60 MAD) – the largest film studios in the world. Continue toward Agdz and Zagora through dramatic desert scenery.
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at your desert camp base near Zagora or M'Hamid. Check into a mid-range desert camp with private tents. Mount camels at sunset for a 45-minute camel trek into the dunes of Erg Chigaga or Erg Lihoudi. Watch the sunset over the Sahara from the top of a sand dune – a truly unforgettable moment.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at the hotel before departure – packed or quick café stop en route
meals.lunch: Roadside Berber restaurant near Aït Benhaddou – lamb tagine with bread and mint tea for ~80–120 MAD
meals.dinner: Traditional Berber dinner at the desert camp – harira soup, tagine, couscous, and Moroccan pastries served under the stars for ~150–200 MAD (often included in camp package)

day_by_day.notes: Book a reputable 3-day Sahara tour through your hotel or a trusted agency in Marrakech (budget ~1,500–2,500 MAD per person for transport, accommodation, and camel ride). Bring warm layers – desert nights in March can drop to 5–10°C. Sunscreen and sunglasses are essential during the day.

day_by_day.morning: Wake before sunrise (around 06:00) to climb the dunes and watch the sunrise paint the Sahara in gold and orange hues – one of Morocco's most magical experiences. After breakfast at camp, visit a local Berber nomad family nearby for an authentic cultural exchange and tea ceremony. Explore the surrounding desert landscape on foot or by 4x4.
day_by_day.afternoon: Begin the return journey toward Marrakech via a different scenic route. Pass through the Todra Gorge – dramatic 300-meter-high limestone canyon walls with a river running through. Take a 1-hour walk through the gorge floor. Continue through the Dades Valley ('Valley of a Thousand Kasbahs') with stops at photogenic mud-brick kasbahs along the route.
day_by_day.evening: Overnight stop in Boumalne Dades or Kelaat M'Gouna (Rose Valley) at a mid-range guesthouse or riad. Stroll through the small town in the evening and enjoy the peaceful contrast to Marrakech's bustle.

meals.breakfast: At the desert camp – Moroccan bread, olive oil, honey, eggs, and mint tea (included in camp package)
meals.lunch: Local restaurant at Todra Gorge – fresh trout from the river (a local specialty), salad, and bread for ~80–120 MAD
meals.dinner: At the guesthouse in Dades Valley – home-cooked Moroccan meal, often a slow-cooked lamb tagine with prunes and almonds for ~100–150 MAD

day_by_day.notes: The Todra Gorge is best visited in the afternoon when light filters dramatically between the canyon walls. If visiting in March, the Rose Valley may have early blooms – the annual Rose Festival is typically in May but the valley is beautiful year-round.

day_by_day.morning: Morning drive back toward Marrakech through the High Atlas Mountains via the Tizi n'Tichka pass (if not taken on Day 4) or the Tizi n'Test pass for a different scenic route. Stop at a Berber mountain village for a short walk and tea with locals. Enjoy the dramatic mountain scenery – snow-capped peaks, terraced fields, and traditional Berber architecture.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive back in Marrakech by early-to-mid afternoon. Check back into Hotel Aday and freshen up. Spend the afternoon revisiting any missed spots in the Medina or exploring the Mouassine neighborhood – one of the Medina's most beautiful quarters with a 16th-century mosque, fountain, and upscale artisan boutiques.
day_by_day.evening: Splurge slightly on a farewell Marrakech dinner at a traditional riad restaurant with live Gnawa music performance. Afterward, take a final evening walk through Jemaa el-Fna to soak in the atmosphere one last time.

meals.breakfast: At the guesthouse in Dades – simple Moroccan breakfast before departure
meals.lunch: Roadside stop in the Atlas Mountains – Berber omelette (kefta or vegetable) with khobz bread and mint tea for ~50–80 MAD
meals.dinner: Dar Zitoun or a similar mid-range riad restaurant in the Medina – full Moroccan feast: pastilla, tagine, couscous, and bastilla au lait dessert for ~200–300 MAD

day_by_day.notes: The drive back from the desert is long (5–7 hours). Use the time to rest and enjoy the scenery. Consider booking the riad dinner in advance as popular spots fill up on weekends.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Marrakech – visit the Ben Youssef Madrasa (entry ~70 MAD), a breathtaking 14th-century Islamic college with intricate zellige tilework, carved stucco, and cedar woodwork. One of the finest examples of Moroccan-Andalusian architecture. Afterward, browse the nearby Mouassine souk for last-minute souvenirs – argan oil, leather goods, Berber rugs, spices, and handmade ceramics.
day_by_day.afternoon: Depending on departure time, enjoy a leisurely lunch in the Medina. Visit the Musée de Marrakech (entry ~50 MAD) housed in a beautiful 19th-century palace if time allows. Pack, check out of the hotel, and arrange airport transfer (petit taxi ~80–100 MAD or pre-booked transfer).
day_by_day.evening: Depart Marrakech with memories of ancient medinas, golden dunes, mountain passes, and the warmth of Moroccan hospitality.

meals.breakfast: Final Moroccan breakfast at Hotel Aday or a nearby café – fresh-squeezed orange juice (Morocco is famous for it), msemen, and mint tea for ~30–50 MAD
meals.lunch: Lunch at Nomad restaurant near the Rahba Kedima souk – modern Moroccan cuisine with rooftop views for ~120–180 MAD
meals.dinner: Airport meal or early dinner before departure

day_by_day.notes: Allow at least 2.5–3 hours before your flight for the taxi ride and airport check-in/security. Marrakech Menara Airport is about 20–25 minutes from the Medina. Declare any argan oil or food products at customs if flying internationally. Keep some MAD for tips and last-minute purchases.

highlights: Mix of paid and free experiences

trip_options.title: Premium Morocco – Marrakech and Sahara Escape
trip_options.description: Indulge in the best the destination has to offer. Premium flights, luxury hotels, and exclusive experiences.

day_by_day.morning: No activities scheduled — late-night arrival. Flight UA lands at 22:30. Private luxury transfer from Marrakech Menara Airport to Hotel Aday in the Medina. A dedicated concierge will greet you at arrivals with a name board. Enjoy a welcome drink and a brief orientation of the riad upon check-in.
day_by_day.afternoon: No activities scheduled — in-flight or transit.
day_by_day.evening: Late-night arrival only. After check-in, unwind with a light welcome platter of Moroccan pastries, mint tea, and seasonal fruits prepared by the hotel. Rest and prepare for the journey ahead.

meals.breakfast: In-flight or at departure airport
meals.lunch: In-flight or at departure airport
meals.dinner: Welcome platter of Moroccan sweets, msemen flatbread, olives, and fresh mint tea arranged by Hotel Aday upon arrival

day_by_day.notes: Arrange a private airport transfer in advance — recommended vehicles include a Mercedes V-Class or similar luxury MPV. Confirm with Hotel Aday that late check-in is prepared. Keep the first night light; no excursions planned. Pack a light layer as Marrakech evenings in March can be cool (12–16°C).

day_by_day.morning: Leisurely breakfast at the riad rooftop terrace. Then embark on a private guided walking tour of the Medina's historic heart: visit the 12th-century Koutoubia Mosque gardens, stroll through the labyrinthine souks of the Mellah (Jewish Quarter), and explore the ornate Ben Youssef Madrasa — one of the largest Islamic colleges in North Africa, featuring stunning Andalusian tilework and carved cedar ceilings.
day_by_day.afternoon: Private guided visit to the Bahia Palace, a 19th-century masterpiece of Moroccan craftsmanship with lush courtyards and painted ceilings. Afterward, explore the Saadian Tombs — royal mausoleums dating to the 16th century, rediscovered only in 1917. End the afternoon with a curated shopping experience in the artisan souks: hand-stitched leather goods, Berber carpets, and silver jewelry, with your guide helping navigate authenticity and fair pricing.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset cocktails on the rooftop of a premier Medina bar (Sky Bar at La Mamounia or Kabana Rooftop). Dinner at Dar Yacout — a legendary Marrakech institution set inside a restored 1930s palace, offering a multi-course traditional Moroccan feast: harira soup, bastilla au pigeon, slow-cooked lamb tagine with preserved lemon, and honey-drenched pastilla for dessert, accompanied by live Gnawa music.

meals.breakfast: Rooftop breakfast at Hotel Aday: fresh-squeezed orange juice, Moroccan pancakes (baghrir), argan oil with honey, assorted pastries, and mint tea
meals.lunch: Lunch at Nomad Restaurant (Derb Aarjan, Medina) — a stylish rooftop bistro blending Moroccan and international flavors; try the lamb merguez briouats and slow-cooked chicken with preserved lemon
meals.dinner: Dar Yacout (1 Rue Sidi Ahmed Soussi) — full traditional Moroccan banquet in a candlelit palace setting; budget approx. 600–900 MAD per person

day_by_day.notes: Ben Youssef Madrasa opens at 09:00. Book Dar Yacout well in advance — it is one of Marrakech's most sought-after dinner experiences. Wear comfortable walking shoes for the Medina cobblestones. A private guide for the day costs approx. 800–1,200 MAD and is highly recommended.

day_by_day.morning: Private half-day excursion to the Majorelle Garden and the adjacent Yves Saint Laurent Museum (Musée Yves Saint Laurent Marrakech). The cobalt-blue Majorelle Garden, restored by YSL and Pierre Bergé, is a botanical sanctuary of rare cacti, bamboo groves, and reflecting pools. The museum showcases the designer's lifelong love affair with Morocco through rotating exhibitions of haute couture and personal archives.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Museum of Moroccan Arts and the Marrakech Museum (Dar Menebhi Palace) in the Medina for a deep dive into Berber jewelry, ancient manuscripts, and traditional costumes. Then enjoy a private hammam and spa ritual at a luxury spa — recommended: the Royal Mansour Spa or Selman Marrakech Spa — featuring a traditional black soap scrub (kessa), argan oil massage, and rose water steam ritual.
day_by_day.evening: Dinner at Le Tobsil (22 Derb Moulay Abdallah Ben Hezzian) — an intimate, candlelit riad restaurant offering a legendary fixed-price Moroccan feast with live Andalusian music. The menu features cold salads, bastilla, lamb mechoui, and a parade of Moroccan desserts. Afterward, a private guided walk through the electric atmosphere of Djemaa el-Fna square at night — snake charmers, storytellers, and food stalls.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at Hotel Aday: fresh fruit platter, Moroccan crepes with amlou (argan oil and almond paste), soft-boiled eggs, and Moroccan coffee
meals.lunch: Light lunch at Café Bousafsaf near Majorelle Garden — fresh salads, Moroccan sandwiches, and freshly squeezed juices in a garden setting
meals.dinner: Le Tobsil — prix-fixe Moroccan banquet approx. 700–900 MAD per person, inclusive of multiple courses and non-alcoholic beverages

day_by_day.notes: Book the Majorelle Garden and YSL Museum tickets online in advance — they sell out quickly, especially in March. The hammam session should be booked 48 hours ahead. Le Tobsil is BYOB (bring your own wine) — purchase a bottle from a licensed shop beforehand if desired.

day_by_day.morning: Depart Marrakech at 07:00 by private luxury 4x4 vehicle (Land Cruiser or similar) for the epic drive to the Sahara Desert via the High Atlas Mountains. Cross the dramatic Tizi n'Tichka Pass (2,260m) with panoramic mountain views. Stop at the UNESCO World Heritage Site of Aït Benhaddou — a breathtaking 11th-century fortified ksar (mud-brick citadel) used as a filming location for Gladiator, Game of Thrones, and Lawrence of Arabia. Enjoy a private guided tour of the ksar with a local Berber historian.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue through the Valley of Roses (Vallée du Dadès) and the dramatic Draa Valley, passing ancient kasbahs, palm oases, and Berber villages. Stop at Skoura Oasis for a brief walk among 1,000-year-old palm groves. Arrive in the Merzouga/Erg Chebbi dune region by late afternoon. Check in to your luxury desert camp or boutique desert lodge (recommended: Scarabeo Camp, Luxury Desert Camp Erg Chebbi, or Kasbah Tombouctou).
day_by_day.evening: Camel trek at golden hour into the Erg Chebbi dunes — the tallest dunes in Morocco at up to 150m. Watch the sunset paint the dunes in shades of amber and crimson from the summit. Return to camp for a traditional Berber dinner under a canopy of stars around a campfire, with live Gnawa and Berber drum music performed by local musicians.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at Hotel Aday before departure: packed Moroccan pastries, fruit, and thermos of mint tea for the road
meals.lunch: Lunch at a traditional Berber restaurant in Aït Benhaddou village — lamb tagine with prunes and almonds, Berber bread, and fresh salads
meals.dinner: Traditional Berber feast at the luxury desert camp: harira soup, mechoui lamb slow-roasted in a clay pit, couscous with seven vegetables, and Moroccan pastries under the stars

day_by_day.notes: The drive from Marrakech to Merzouga is approximately 8–9 hours with stops — an early departure is essential. Dress in layers; the High Atlas can be cold in March mornings, while the desert afternoon is warm (20–25°C) but nights drop to 5–8°C. Bring a warm jacket, sunscreen, and a scarf for the dunes. Confirm camel trek and camp arrangements 48 hours in advance.

day_by_day.morning: Wake before dawn for a private sunrise camel or 4x4 excursion to the highest dune crest in Erg Chebbi — witnessing the Sahara sunrise is one of the most extraordinary experiences in the world. Return to camp for a leisurely breakfast. Optional: sandboarding on the dunes or a guided quad bike excursion across the desert landscape. Visit a nearby Gnawa musician's home for a private cultural music session and tea ceremony.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the village of Merzouga and the Khamlia village — home to the Gnawa people, descendants of sub-Saharan African slaves, renowned for their hypnotic spiritual music. Enjoy a private concert and mint tea with a local Gnawa family. Explore the fossil and mineral markets of Erfoud — Morocco's 'fossil capital,' where trilobites and ammonites dating 350 million years are carved and polished by local artisans.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the luxury desert camp or lodge for a private stargazing session with a telescope guided by a local astronomer — the Sahara offers some of the darkest skies in the world. Dinner at the camp featuring a refined Moroccan-Berber menu with premium ingredients. Retire early for a restful night in a luxury desert suite or furnished Berber tent.

meals.breakfast: Full Berber breakfast at camp: msemen flatbreads, honey, argan oil, fresh dates, Moroccan coffee, and mint tea served in the dunes at sunrise
meals.lunch: Lunch at a local Berber family home in Merzouga — a curated cultural dining experience featuring homemade tagine, fresh bread baked in a clay oven, and seasonal salads (arranged by your guide)
meals.dinner: Gourmet dinner at the luxury desert camp: slow-cooked lamb shoulder, saffron-infused couscous, roasted vegetable salads, and almond bastilla for dessert

day_by_day.notes: Sunrise is approximately 07:15 in mid-March — set an alarm for 06:00. Bring a headlamp for pre-dawn navigation in the dunes. The Khamlia village visit should be arranged through your guide to ensure a respectful and authentic experience. Tipping local musicians and hosts is customary and appreciated.

day_by_day.morning: Depart the desert camp at 08:00 for the return journey to Marrakech via an alternative scenic route through the Todra Gorge — a spectacular canyon with 300m-high rose-red limestone walls, one of Morocco's most dramatic natural wonders. Enjoy a guided walk through the narrowest section of the gorge alongside a crystal-clear mountain stream.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue through the Dadès Gorge (Valley of a Thousand Kasbahs) — a winding road flanked by ancient mud-brick fortresses and dramatic rock formations. Stop at a traditional Berber cooperative in the Rose Valley (Vallée des Roses) to learn about the distillation of rose water and argan oil — Morocco's liquid gold. Purchase premium rose water, argan oil, and rose-infused cosmetics directly from the cooperative. Arrive back in Marrakech by early evening.
day_by_day.evening: Relaxing evening in Marrakech. Enjoy a private rooftop dinner at La Maison Arabe (1 Derb Assehbe, Bab Doukkala) — one of Marrakech's oldest and most celebrated restaurants, offering refined Moroccan cuisine in an intimate candlelit courtyard setting. Post-dinner: a leisurely stroll through the illuminated Djemaa el-Fna square.

meals.breakfast: Packed breakfast from the desert camp: dates, Moroccan pastries, and thermos of mint tea for the road
meals.lunch: Lunch at a scenic restaurant overlooking the Todra Gorge — grilled kefta, Berber tagine, and fresh mountain spring water
meals.dinner: La Maison Arabe, Marrakech — refined Moroccan tasting menu featuring bastilla au pigeon, lamb tagine with ras el hanout, and orange blossom crème brûlée; approx. 700–1,000 MAD per person

day_by_day.notes: The return drive via Todra Gorge adds approximately 1–2 hours compared to the direct route but is highly recommended for its scenery. Arrive at the gorge before 11:00 to avoid tour group crowds. Confirm your Marrakech hotel reservation for the return night. La Maison Arabe dinner reservation should be made in advance.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Marrakech. Enjoy a slow, indulgent breakfast at the riad. Visit the El Badi Palace ruins — a 16th-century palace once described as one of the wonders of the world, now a hauntingly beautiful ruin with stork nests atop its towers and a sunken orange grove. Explore the attached Museum of Moroccan Carpets and Textiles. Final souvenir shopping in the Mellah spice market — purchase premium saffron, ras el hanout spice blends, and argan oil to take home.
day_by_day.afternoon: Farewell luxury hammam session at your hotel or a nearby premium spa — a final indulgent ritual of steam, black soap, and rose water to refresh before travel. Return to the hotel for packing and checkout. Enjoy a final mint tea on the riad rooftop, savoring the sounds and scents of the Medina.
day_by_day.evening: Private luxury transfer to Marrakech Menara Airport. Departure lounge: if time permits, enjoy a final Moroccan pastry and coffee at the airport café. Carry home memories of ancient kasbahs, golden dunes, and the warmth of Moroccan hospitality.

meals.breakfast: Farewell breakfast at Hotel Aday: full spread of Moroccan specialties — amlou, honey, msemen, fresh fruit, Moroccan coffee, and mint tea
meals.lunch: Lunch at Café des Épices (75 Rahba Lakdima, Spice Square) — a beloved Medina rooftop café with views over the spice market; try the zaalouk (smoky eggplant dip), kefta sandwich, and fresh lemonade with orange blossom
meals.dinner: Light pre-departure dinner or airport dining — alternatively, an early dinner at Pepe Nero (18 Derb Cherkaoui, Douar Graoua) — a sophisticated Italian-Moroccan fusion restaurant in a stunning riad setting, ideal for a relaxed final evening

day_by_day.notes: Check out time at Hotel Aday is typically 12:00 — arrange a late checkout (14:00–15:00) if your flight is in the evening. Allow at least 2.5 hours before departure for airport transfer and check-in. Marrakech Menara Airport is approximately 20–30 minutes from the Medina by private car. Declare any argan oil or food products at customs if returning to the EU or US.
